title: Ask events
description: Every event the ask service emits on a ticket's stream. One schema per event type; the stream is the union. Client-agnostic by construction: nothing here is rendered text for any particular surface, and no event but `accepted` carries the caller's question.

seq.description: Monotonic per ticket, no gaps. Doubles as the SSE `id:` field, so `Last-Event-ID: <seq>` resumes from seq+1.

question.description: The question as received. This is the ONLY event that carries it; a client that stores events may store everything but this one and hold no natural language.

turn.description: 1-based position of this ask within its conversation.

branch.description: A unit of work opened or closed. Phase 1 emits exactly one per ticket, wrapping the whole run, so clients handle branches before fan-out exists. Phase 2 emits one per sub-agent, derived from the configured sources, never from a hand-written roster.

source.description: A name from `list_sources`, or null for the supervisor's own branch.

role.description: What the branch is for. `source` branches carry a `source`; the others do not.

step.description: One tool call, as it happened. DIAGNOSTIC: for traces, evals and audit reconciliation. A client should not show this to a person unless they asked to see the work. Droppable on stream overflow.

tool.description: Namespaced as the agent sees it, e.g. `warehouse__run_query`.

args.description: As sent. A refused call's args are kept: the refusal is the evidence.

ms.description: Matches the executor's audit line for the same call.

is_error.description: The tool returned `isError`. A refusal, not a transport failure.

milestone.description: Progress a person could be told. STRUCTURED, never prose: the client renders it in its own words, length and language. Never dropped on overflow.

phase.description: grounding: reading the catalog for meaning. discovering: finding tables or operations. querying: a statement or call is running. reconciling: results are being brought together.

subject.description: What the phase is about, in the catalog's vocabulary: a glossary term, a metric, a table's display name. Never the question.

answer.description: Terminal. The agent ran something and has a result. Fields rather than prose so every client renders in its own order with its own limits; `text` is kept so a text client prints exactly what the CLI prints today.

path.description: How the answer was reached, split so a client can act on it without knowing this service's domain. `speed` is the general fact -- `fast` means nothing beyond metadata was consulted and the answer arrives in a fraction of the time; `full` means the sources were queried. A client builds latency policy on `speed` alone. `detail` names what actually answered in this service's own vocabulary and is for display and diagnostics; a client that switches on it is coupling itself to a warehouse.

speed.description: `fast`: no statement or call ran. `full`: at least one did.

detail.description: `catalog`: the catalog alone. `warehouse`: one source. `multi`: more than one source, or a divergence arm.

headline.description: Present only when one figure is the salient result. Most answers are a table and have none.

label.description: In the catalog's words where it has them.

provenance.description: Every stated meaning the answer depends on, and where each was read from. In this service they are catalog definitions; the shape is deliberately general, because "the answer rests on these stated meanings, from these sources" is what a client renders and it is true of more than a glossary. Empty when the catalog was withheld, which is what makes the attribution metric scoreable.

statement.description: The definition, as the source words it.

source.description: The entity it was read from -- an OpenMetadata FQN here.

kind.description: What sort of statement this is, in the service's vocabulary: `glossary_term`, `metric`, `column_description`. A client may show it; it must not depend on the set.

sql.description: Every statement that ran, as the executor reported it.

caveats.description: What the catalog itself raised: a deprecation tag, a disputed definition, a known gap. Short, one per item. A client that speaks must say these; a client that renders must show them.

divergence.description: Reserved for phase 2: what the answer would have been without the catalog, and why it differs. Always null in phase 1.

abstention.description: Terminal. The agent looked and concluded the data could not answer: no statement ran and nothing was refused. Mechanical, the same rule as `Answer.abstained`. Carries the catalog vocabulary tried, never the question, so a client can forward it to a steward without forwarding what was asked.

refusal.description: Terminal. A tool refused: the caller lacks access, or a guard declined the statement. A security event, and a different outcome from an answer, so a client can never narrate it as one. Says what was refused, never what the caller would have seen.

what.description: access: the source or a rule withheld it. guard: the statement or call was not admissible. rate_limit: the gateway refused the call.

detail.description: The refusing tool's own message, which is already written not to leak.

error.description: Terminal. Something failed that is not a refusal: a transport error, a model error, the step ceiling, a cancel. Distinct from `refusal` because it is not a security event and a client should say so differently.

done.description: Always the last event, exactly once, after any terminal event. Usage for the run.

hops.description: Model calls made. Equals the number of `step` events only when each hop made one tool call.

steps.description: Tool calls made. Equals the number of `step` events emitted, before any overflow drop.
